HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P)

History:
• Chief complaint: Recurrent episodes of right-hand pins/needles with right-sided weakness  
• Onset/progression: Began ≈1.5–2 months ago; initially once/week to once/month, now occurring several times/day. Each episode lasts 3-4 days then resolves.  
• Character/associated symptoms during episodes:  
  – Numbness/pins-and-needles confined to right hand  
  – Subjective weakness of right arm and right leg; colleagues note abnormal gait  
  – Difficulty holding/drinking a cup of coffee  
  – Sensation of “something in throat” but no true dysphagia  
  – No dysarthria, no visual disturbance, no persistent swallowing difficulty outside episodes  
  – General fatigue and occasional nausea between episodes  
• Current status: Asymptomatic at time of consultation  
• Family history: Father underwent carotid surgery to reduce stroke risk  
• Social: 32-year-old plastic-surgery doctor; lives with wife; non-smoker  
• Review of systems otherwise unremarkable (per transcript)

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses reported  
• Surgical history: none mentioned  
• Medications: Aspirin 75 mg once daily (dose/route/frequency not documented by clinician; self-started)  
• Allergies: Penicillin (reaction not specified)

Physical Examination:
(Conducted via video/telephone; no direct exam possible)  
• General: Alert, oriented, speaking normally; no deficits observed during call  
• Neurologic: Patient reports no active weakness or sensory loss at time of consult  
• No other physical findings documented

Impression:
Recurrent transient focal neurological deficits concerning for transient ischaemic attacks (TIAs).

Management Plan:
• Urgent referral to TIA (mini-stroke) clinic; referral sent today with request for review within 24–48 hours.  
• Anticipated tests at clinic: carotid Doppler ultrasound, brain imaging, and other stroke work-up.  
• Emergency advice: If symptoms recur and are prolonged, attend A&E immediately.  
• Contact information (PALS and TIA clinic numbers) provided; patient advised to phone later today or tomorrow morning to confirm appointment and ensure timely review.  
• Medication: No immediate change to self-initiated aspirin; will be reviewed by stroke team.  
• Follow-up: Patient to update GP if appointment delayed or if new/worsening events occur.

Patient Summary:
A 32-year-old male doctor with a 1.5-month history of episodic right-sided sensory and motor symptoms, now increasing in frequency, likely representing TIAs. Referred urgently to stroke/TIA clinic for expedited imaging and vascular assessment.

Key Takeaways:
1. Attend the TIA clinic within the next 1–2 days as arranged.  
2. Go directly to A&E if an episode occurs that does not resolve quickly.  
3. Call the provided clinic numbers today/tomorrow to confirm the appointment; contact GP if any delays.

Next Steps:
• Complete stroke clinic evaluation (carotid ultrasound, brain scan, blood work).  
• Review need for ongoing antiplatelet therapy and risk-factor modification after specialist assessment.  
• GP to follow up once clinic results available.
